item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. SCOPe 2.08 places these groups in three distinct superfamilies within fold f.21, “Heme-binding four-helical bundle” (SUNID 81344): transmembrane di-heme cytochromes, f.21.1 (81342); fumarate reductase respiratory-complex transmembrane subunits, f.21.2 (81343); and respiratory nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain, f.21.3 (103501). Their shared class is f, “Membrane and cell surface proteins and peptides.” These are separate superfamilies, not merely separate families within one superfamily. Family membership supports closer evolutionary relationships; superfamily membership supports probable common ancestry; shared fold and class alone do not establish homology. The common heme-binding architecture therefore does not justify merging these groups or transferring substrate specificity, respiratory-complex role, or detailed mechanism between them. A cross-superfamily structural template may suggest overall architecture, but requires validation of sequence correspondence, topology, heme ligation, and functional sites. Separate superfamilies do not prove independent origins: establishing deeper homology would require additional sequence/profile, detailed structural, and evolutionary evidence beyond the shared bundle.","evidence_used":["Pretrained knowledge of SCOPe hierarchy and homology inference","mcp__scope__search_scop","mcp__scope__get_scop_node","mcp__scope__list_scop_children","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=di-heme&mode=auto&limit=30","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=fumarate&mode=auto&limit=30","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=nitrate&mode=auto&limit=30","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344/children?limit=20"]}]}
